docs.purpose: Optionally asks which supplier the user mainly buys from, offering a grid of the common names for their trade plus a free-text box for anything else. It can be skipped entirely. If there are no known suppliers for that trade, the screen skips itself automatically and the user never sees it.
docs.data_story: It reads nothing from the database directly. Every value arrives through 2 contracts: `/api/onboarding/suppliers`, `/api/user-profile`. Behind those contracts, the data comes from `entitlements`, `trade_suppliers` and `user_profiles`, and writes land on `entitlements` and `user_profiles`. It also holds client-side state in `onboardingStore` and `filterStore`, which is the part a server-driven projection has to absorb or justify. It emits **no analytics event**, so nothing it does is currently countable.
docs.under_126: **REBUILD** — it holds Layer-3 state (`onboardingStore` and `filterStore`) and drives writes, so a client decision has to be re-homed on the server before the projection can be honest. It renders through the WIZARD_STEP renderer (declared step index, advance condition, resume key and skip rule), reading by reference: `/api/onboarding/suppliers`, `/api/user-profile`. It owns no component of its own, so its `owns.components[]` is an empty array — a legal answer, written down.

emits: mobile/app/(onboarding)/supplier.tsx:1-213 — no track() call in the file

identity.owner: unassigned (no CODEOWNERS file and no owner registry exists in the repo — measured 2026-09-15)

versioning.why: The suppliers response is a bare { data: { suppliers: string[] } } with no Zod mirror on either side — a local interface only, so both ends move together in one commit.

inputs.why: GET /api/onboarding/suppliers?trade= supplies the grid, keyed on the canonical filterStore.tradeSlug; the free-text "Other" box is the only non-contract input.

evidence: migrations/113_trade_suppliers.sql:23 — the rows are INSERTed by the migration seed
docs/reference/data-lineage-map.md — table absent from the generated map (checked 2026-09-15)

outputs.why: The selection PATCHes first and only then writes filterStore.setSupplierSelection; Skip deliberately writes nothing at all, so the step advances without a server round-trip.
outputs.rollback: none needed — the local mirror is written only after the PATCH resolves; a failure renders "Could not save. Please try again." and the step does not advance.

state.why: It reads the MMKV-persisted filterStore.tradeSlug to key the query (so a cold boot mid-onboarding still resolves the right supplier list) and writes supplierSelection back into the same store.

fields.canonical_writer: mobile_onboarding_path (and profession, for the realtor shortcut)

fields.canonical_writer: this surface, after the PATCH confirms

staleness.why: The supplier list inherits the global 5-minute staleTime — no per-hook override — which is harmless because the step is visited once.

session.why: The step is only reachable once AuthGate has a Supabase user whose server profile says onboarding_complete is false; PATCH /api/user-profile is an authenticated route.

rls_class.why: trade_suppliers is not in the Class-A list and is read as table owner through the route; the write target, user_profiles, is Class A.

checks.why: When the query resolves with zero suppliers the step auto-skips to the next screen rather than rendering an empty grid; the guard on selectedTrade prevents a premature skip while the store rehydrates (supplier.tsx:59-66).
A failed PATCH renders "Could not save. Please try again." above the CTA and the step does not advance (supplier.tsx:129-133, 183-185).

Measured absence: the response is typed with a local interface and read as data?.data?.suppliers ?? [] — a drifted shape becomes an empty list, which the auto-skip then treats as "this trade has no suppliers".

errors.why: One inline red line above the CTA; a failed supplier LIST fetch has no rendering at all and degrades into the auto-skip path.

emits.why: No event fires, so neither the supplier chosen nor the skip rate is measurable — which is the one thing Spec 87's supplier-audience work would need.

offers.why: No sponsored placement is rendered: the only slot component in the Expo tree is SponsorSlot, and it returns null unless EXPO_PUBLIC_PARCEL_SPONSORS=1.

metering.why: Nothing here is counted: the Spec 126 §7 usage ledger table does not exist (grep for usage_events in the introspected drizzle schema returns 0 hits), and the only quota-shaped counter, user_profiles.lead_views_count, is incremented solely by POST /api/leads/view, which has no mobile caller.

config.why: The surface consumes no registered logic variable: the only server-side tunable in this path, user_profiles.radius_cap_km, is a per-user admin column, not a logic_variables row.

sharing.why: PATCH /api/user-profile is rendered by every onboarding step, both shells, settings and the filter sheet — it is the most-shared contract in the mobile estate.

limitations.what: A supplier-list fetch error is indistinguishable from "this trade has no suppliers": both land on the auto-skip.
limitations.measured: supplier.tsx:45-66 never reads isError; suppliers defaults to [] and the effect fires router.replace on length 0.

limitations.what: Only the Confirm CTA carries an accessibility attribute (role); the supplier tiles, the Other field and Skip carry none.

notes: This is the only onboarding step with an inbound contract, and it reaches it with a useQuery whose queryFn is a bare fetchWithAuth — the PATCH on the same screen has no hook at all.

programme.why: Onboarding writes `user_profiles` columns both products read; the flow is shared even though its copy is lead-gen-shaped today.
